# 📁 Organize Your Paper Files

## 🎯 Current Situation

You have **two sets** of JSON files:

1. **Codex Files** (Current local files) - Generated by Codex/AI
2. **OG Files** (On GitHub repo) - Your original good files

## 📋 Step-by-Step Organization

### Step 1: Backup Current "Codex" Files

```powershell
# Create folder for Codex-generated files
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path "public/papers-codex" -Force

# Move current files to codex folder
Move-Item "public/papers/*.json" -Destination "public/papers-codex/" -Force

# Keep sample_test.json in main folder (it's good)
Copy-Item "public/papers-codex/sample_test.json" -Destination "public/papers/" -Force
```

**Result:** Current files are now in `public/papers-codex/`

### Step 2: Download "OG" Files from GitHub

#### Option A: Using Git (Recommended)

```bash
# Fetch latest from GitHub
git fetch origin

# Get the papers from GitHub (without affecting other files)
git checkout origin/main -- public/papers/

# This downloads your OG files from GitHub
```

#### Option B: Manual Download from GitHub

1. Go to your GitHub repo
2. Navigate to `public/papers/`
3. Download each JSON file you want
4. Save to `public/papers-og/` folder

```powershell
# Create OG folder
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path "public/papers-og" -Force

# Download from GitHub (replace with your repo URL)
$baseUrl = "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/YOUR_USERNAME/YOUR_REPO/main/public/papers"
$papers = @(
    "0417_s20_qp_11.json",
    "0417_s20_qp_12.json",
    "0417_s21_qp_12.json"
    # Add more papers...
)

foreach ($paper in $papers) {
    $url = "$baseUrl/$paper"
    $output = "public/papers-og/$paper"
    Invoke-WebRequest -Uri $url -OutFile $output
    Write-Host "Downloaded: $paper"
}
```

### Step 3: Compare Both Versions

Now you have:
```
public/
├── papers/              (Empty, ready for your choice)
├── papers-codex/        (AI-generated files)
└── papers-og/           (Your original GitHub files)
```

### Step 4: Test Both Versions

#### Test Codex Files

```powershell
# Copy codex files to main folder
Copy-Item "public/papers-codex/*.json" -Destination "public/papers/" -Force

# Start server
npm run dev

# Test at: http://localhost:3000/practice/0417_s20_qp_11
```

Take screenshots of papers you like!

#### Test OG Files

```powershell
# Clear main folder
Remove-Item "public/papers/*.json" -Exclude "sample_test.json"

# Copy OG files to main folder
Copy-Item "public/papers-og/*.json" -Destination "public/papers/" -Force

# Refresh browser (Ctrl+Shift+R)
# Test at: http://localhost:3000/practice/0417_s20_qp_11
```

Take screenshots of papers you like!

### Step 5: Create Comparison Report

```powershell
# Create a comparison script
$report = @()

# Get all paper names
$allPapers = (Get-ChildItem "public/papers-codex/*.json").Name | Sort-Object -Unique

foreach ($paper in $allPapers) {
    $codexPath = "public/papers-codex/$paper"
    $ogPath = "public/papers-og/$paper"
    
    $codexSize = if (Test-Path $codexPath) { 
        [math]::Round((Get-Item $codexPath).Length/1KB, 2) 
    } else { 0 }
    
    $ogSize = if (Test-Path $ogPath) { 
        [math]::Round((Get-Item $ogPath).Length/1KB, 2) 
    } else { 0 }
    
    $report += [PSCustomObject]@{
        Paper = $paper
        CodexKB = $codexSize
        OG_KB = $ogSize
        HasCodex = Test-Path $codexPath
        HasOG = Test-Path $ogPath
    }
}

$report | Format-Table -AutoSize
$report | Export-Csv "paper-comparison.csv" -NoTypeInformation
Write-Host "`nReport saved to: paper-comparison.csv"
```

### Step 6: Choose Best Version for Each Paper

Create a decision file `PAPER_DECISIONS.md`:

```markdown
# Paper Version Decisions

## 0417_s20_qp_11.json
- Codex: 85 KB, text clean, tables work ✅
- OG: 120 KB, text perfect, all features ⭐
- **Decision**: Use OG

## 0417_s20_qp_12.json
- Codex: 2 KB, empty ❌
- OG: 95 KB, good ✅
- **Decision**: Use OG

## 0417_s21_qp_12.json
- Codex: 110 KB, excellent ⭐
- OG: 0 KB, missing ❌
- **Decision**: Use Codex

(Continue for each paper...)
```

### Step 7: Build Final Collection

Based on your decisions, copy the best version of each paper:

```powershell
# Clear main folder
Remove-Item "public/papers/*.json" -Exclude "sample_test.json"

# Copy best versions (example)
Copy-Item "public/papers-og/0417_s20_qp_11.json" -Destination "public/papers/"
Copy-Item "public/papers-og/0417_s20_qp_12.json" -Destination "public/papers/"
Copy-Item "public/papers-codex/0417_s21_qp_12.json" -Destination "public/papers/"
# ... continue for each paper
```

## 🎨 Visual Comparison Tool

Create a simple HTML file to compare side-by-side:

```html
<!-- Save as compare.html in project root -->
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
<head>
    <title>Paper Comparison</title>
    <style>
        body { font-family: Arial; padding: 20px; }
        .container { display: flex; gap: 20px; }
        .version { flex: 1; border: 1px solid #ccc; padding: 10px; }
        .version h2 { background: #f0f0f0; padding: 10px; }
        pre { background: #f9f9f9; padding: 10px; overflow: auto; max-height: 600px; }
    </style>
</head>
<body>
    <h1>Paper Comparison Tool</h1>
    <div class="container">
        <div class="version">
            <h2>Codex Version</h2>
            <pre id="codex"></pre>
        </div>
        <div class="version">
            <h2>OG Version</h2>
            <pre id="og"></pre>
        </div>
    </div>
    <script>
        const paper = prompt("Enter paper name (e.g., 0417_s20_qp_11.json):");
        
        fetch(`/papers-codex/${paper}`)
            .then(r => r.json())
            .then(data => {
                document.getElementById('codex').textContent = JSON.stringify(data, null, 2);
            });
        
        fetch(`/papers-og/${paper}`)
            .then(r => r.json())
            .then(data => {
                document.getElementById('og').textContent = JSON.stringify(data, null, 2);
            });
    </script>
</body>
</html>
```

## 📊 Quick Decision Matrix

| Criteria | Codex Files | OG Files |
|----------|-------------|----------|
| **Text Quality** | Good (normalized) | Excellent (original) |
| **Tables** | Auto-detected | Manually verified |
| **Question Types** | AI-inferred | Accurate |
| **Completeness** | May have gaps | Complete |
| **File Size** | Varies | Consistent |

## 🎯 Recommended Strategy

### For Each Paper:

1. **Check OG first** - If it exists and looks good, use it
2. **Check Codex** - If OG is missing or broken, use Codex
3. **Test both** - If both exist, test and choose better one
4. **Hybrid approach** - Use OG for most, Codex for missing ones

### Priority Order:

1. ⭐ **OG files** (your proven good files)
2. ✅ **Codex files** (if OG missing or broken)
3. 🔄 **Re-convert from Supabase** (if both are bad)

## 🚀 Final Setup Command

Once you've decided, create a setup script:

```powershell
# setup-final-papers.ps1

# Clear main folder
Remove-Item "public/papers/*.json" -Exclude "sample_test.json"

# Copy your chosen versions
# (Edit this list based on your decisions)

# Use OG for these:
$ogPapers = @(
    "0417_s20_qp_11.json",
    "0417_s20_qp_12.json"
)
foreach ($paper in $ogPapers) {
    Copy-Item "public/papers-og/$paper" -Destination "public/papers/"
}

# Use Codex for these:
$codexPapers = @(
    "0417_s21_qp_12.json"
)
foreach ($paper in $codexPapers) {
    Copy-Item "public/papers-codex/$paper" -Destination "public/papers/"
}

Write-Host "✅ Final paper collection ready!"
Get-ChildItem "public/papers/*.json" | Measure-Object | Select-Object Count
```
